caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
data_source: IMF World Economic Outlook via DataMapper (latest vintage, accessed October 2026)
debt_management: The DRC's debt was erased by HIPC/MDRI relief in 2010: from 107.5% of GDP in 2006 it collapsed to 7.6% by 2012, the series low. The post-relief government borrowed cautiously at first, and the ratio stayed under 16% through 2024, one of Africa's lowest. It is now climbing as the government taps regional and international markets to fund infrastructure: 19.9% projected for 2025. Sustainability is comfortable on paper, but that reflects how little the state borrows, not fiscal strength; domestic revenue mobilization is among the world's weakest, and the real fiscal story is off-budget mining deals and chronic under-spending on public goods.
inflation_management: The DRC's inflation record is a series of currency crises. It hit 46.1% in 2009 as the global crisis crushed mining revenues and the franc, then stabilized remarkably to 0.7-1.2% in 2013-2015 under tighter policy. The 2016-18 political crisis around Kabila's succession brought a second collapse: 35.7% in 2017 and 29.3% in 2018. The central bank stabilized the franc after 2019, bringing inflation to 4.7%, but depreciation resumed in 2022-24 (19.9% in 2023, 17.7% in 2024) on fiscal slippages and conflict. It eased to a projected 7.4% in 2025. There is no inflation-targeting framework; policy is essentially exchange-rate defense with limited reserves.

key_events.event: Global crisis crushed copper/cobalt prices; inflation hit 46.1% as the franc collapsed.
HIPC completion-point relief cut debt from 107.5% to under 10% of GDP.
Political crisis over Kabila's refusal to step down; inflation surged to 35.7% (2017) amid franc depreciation.
Felix Tshisekedi took office after disputed elections; mining code revised to capture more revenue.
COVID-19, then Ukraine war: franc depreciation pushed inflation to 19.9% in 2023.
Tshisekedi re-elected (December 2023); M23 rebellion seized territory in the east, straining the budget.

outlook_next_decade: The base case is mining-led growth with low debt but persistent inflation risk from the franc. Upside is enormous: cobalt, copper, and lithium demand could transform revenues if governance improves; downside is that it won't, and conflict in the east keeps the economy fragmented. Uncertainty is high: macro stability depends on commodity prices and politics far more than on policy frameworks, which remain weak.
